chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ibn Muskān from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, referring to Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ابْنُ مُسْكَانَ: Ibn Muskān, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٌ الْحَلَبِيُّ: Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Like it, indicating the content is identical to the previous narration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling regarding the divorce narration transmitted by Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī?
ai.summary: This concise narration in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* utilizes the chain of Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī to transmit the legal ruling of Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him), affirming its consistency with the preceding text on divorce. It highlights the rigorous isnad (chain of transmission) methodology characteristic of Shia jurisprudence, where the reliability of narrators like al-Ḥalabī ensures the authenticity of the fiqh derived from the Imams. This linkage underscores the continuity of legal principles within the chapter of Ṭalāq, reinforcing the established rulings on marital dissolution.
